scope: Native application executor replacement: the per-node TypeScript BrepSemanticBackend (src/services/brepSemanticBackend.ts, 329 lines) is deleted; the native graph/session executor (brepNativeExecutor.ts -> brep_session graph-begin/graph-advance/graph-commit) is the only B-rep execution path, and the displayPolicyHash derivation moves behind the WASM ABI as the new brep_scene_plan op
coverage: Deleted TypeScript executor state, all of it duplicated by the native session: the payloadEntries WeakMap with frozen host geometry snapshots, the per-session entries/issued/localPayloads lease maps and sets, the host-side nativeLease translation table, the host-side programHash/languageContract/carrierKey/nodeIndex consistency checks (Rust already re-derives carrier/evidence admission and input order per node), the retained-set commit re-validation (duplicates/foreign/released refused natively at commit), and the abort-on-failure session disposal chain; Rust owns every lease, snapshot, commit, and disposal decision

Deleted with it: the BrepSemanticPayload symbol-brand, BREP_SEMANTIC_CARRIERS, inspectBrepSemanticPayload/inspectBrepSemanticProfilePayload snapshot views, and the maxRetainedGeometryCharacters host knob (a test-only lowering of the 4 MiB bound; the native session enforces maxCharacters itself and the graph path always uses MAX_NATIVE_GEOMETRY_CHARACTERS)

Audit result: no production src/ caller of createBrepSemanticBackend existed; the scene path (brepSemanticScene.ts -> executeBrepNativeProgram) was already fully native, so only tests consumed the legacy backend. BrepSemanticBackendError stays in brepSemanticErrors.ts as the host diagnostic shape for native failure reports

displayPolicyHash migrated natively: new brep_scene_plan op (brep_scene_plan.rs) validates quality in {preview,full} and segments in 1..32 and derives sha256('brep-display-policy-v1\n' + canonical policy JSON) byte-identically to the retired host derivation (pinned hash test: preview/4 = ec733240...a97b); brepSemanticScene.ts consumes displayPlan.displayPolicyHash and keeps its RangeError guard so the public error surface is unchanged. The diagnostic lane (brepDiagnosticProtocol.ts diagnosticDisplayPolicyHash) deliberately keeps its host-side re-derivation so a compromised worker cannot self-certify its own policy

Mesh-span/provenance mapping in brepSemanticScene.ts stays host-side as pure bookkeeping: spans are copied verbatim from the admitted envelope (provenanceByOperation lookup), entity IDs come from natively admitted occurrence.sceneEntityId, and no arithmetic is involved

brepNativeExecutor.ts error surface preserved: the brep-1 contract refusal now carries backendCause E_BREP_SEMANTIC_UNSUPPORTED exactly as the legacy backend did, and native failure reports reconstruct GeometryKernelError as backendCause.kernelCause so kernel-failure consumers observe the identical shape
NativeValue now exposes valueType (already present on the wire) so consumers can assert representation-preserving evidence without a host payload view

Test migration, no assertions weakened: tests/brepNativeProgramSemantics.test.ts (17 tests) ports every geometry and behavior assertion of the retired 18-test brepSemanticBackend suite to executeBrepNativeProgram — exact primitives/transforms/booleans/profiles/extrusions, deep-freeze and mutation refusal, empty-typing, facet-intent independence, unsupported-carrier/operation refusals with mapped backendCause codes, abort-between-steps with unrelated-snapshot preservation, structuredClone minted-artifact refusal, and the node-budget refusal; the two backend-independent brep_semantic_geometry endpoint tests carry over verbatim; lease-lifecycle cases that tested deleted TS APIs are covered natively by brepNativeSession.test.ts (foreign/released/swapped handles, commit retention, disposal revocation) and the brep_session/brep_session_abi Rust suites (budget restoration, foreign sessions, duplicate handles)

tests/brepNativeSession.test.ts no longer cross-checks against the legacy executor; it asserts exact geometry instead (difference(){cube(3);cube(1);} -> one body, volume 26 mm3). tests/brepProfileExtrusionAudit.test.ts runs its five audit cases through executeBrepNativeProgram with identical mass/centroid/refusal assertions
behaviorChange: All B-rep semantics execute in one native graph/session pass with Rust-owned leases; the host keeps transport plus UI bookkeeping only (selection, entity IDs, display mesh assembly, presentation metadata). Public behavior is unchanged: identical scene output, identical mapped error codes (E_SEMANTIC_BACKEND_FAILURE/BEGIN/BUDGET/ABORTED with BrepSemanticBackendError causes), identical refusal cases, identical displayPolicyHash values
limitations: The per-node incremental API surface (evaluate/releasePayload/validatePayload per node with mid-session snapshot inspection) is gone by design: no production caller used it, and the native session covers the same lifecycle rules at the wire level; any future consumer needing mid-graph snapshots must use brep_session begin/evaluate/snapshot/commit directly, not a host payload cache

The maxRetainedGeometryCharacters test knob is retired; character-budget exhaustion is now exercised only at the native fixed 4 MiB bound (covered by Rust session tests, not reachable through executeBrepNativeProgram without an oversized program)

Display tessellation (prepareBrepDisplay), BVH/edge extraction, geometryAssetId, and the 20,000-triangle display budget remain host-side presentation concerns; brep_scene_plan owns only policy admission and hash derivation
The native executor still cannot evaluate hull nodes or curved booleans (pre-existing gap, unchanged): admitted hull programs refuse with E_BREP_SEMANTIC_UNSUPPORTED
The generic executeSemanticProgram host executor remains in place for the Manifold backend (manifoldPlanBackend.ts), which is out of scope for the B-rep migration
